results.title: Mastering Latency Compensation
results.content: Client-side prediction is a technique where the client predicts the outcome of a player's action and renders the result immediately, while also sending the action to the server for validation. The client corrects its local state based on the server's response ### Implementing Movement Prediction and Correction To implement movement prediction, the client can use the following formula to predict the new position: \[ \mathbf{p)_{predicted} = \mathbf{p)_{current} + \mathbf{v)_{current} \times \Delta t \] where \( \mathbf{p\)_{current} ) is the current position, \( \mathbf{v\)_{current} ) is the current velocity, and Δ t \Delta t Δ t is the time since the last update. ### Techniques for Reconciling Client and Server States There are several techniques for reconciling client and server states, including: ### Best Practices for Minimizing Discrepancies To minimize discrepancies between the client and server states, developers can: * Use high-frequency updates for critical state information * Implement robust error correction mechanisms * Optimize server processing time to reduce latency In addition to client-side prediction and server-side reconciliation, there are several advanced latency compensation methods that can be used to further improve responsiveness and reduce lag. * Interpolation: estimating the state between two known states * Extrapolation: predicting the future state based on current and past states ### Implementing Lag Compensation for Shooting Mechanics Lag compensation for shooting mechanics involves predicting the position of targets and adjusting the client's rendering accordingly. * First-person shooters: lag compensation for shooting mechanics * Racing games: client-side prediction for vehicle movement * Fighting games: precise timing and input prediction To optimize latency compensation, developers should consider the following best practices: ### Tips for Optimizing Latency Compensation in Different Network Conditions * Use adaptive latency compensation techniques that adjust to changing network conditions * Optimize server processing time to reduce latency * Implement robust error correction mechanisms ### Balancing Between Responsiveness and Accuracy Developers must balance between responsiveness and accuracy when implementing latency compensation techniques. A: Latency compensation refers to the techniques used to mitigate the effects of latency in online gaming, improving responsiveness and reducing lag. A: Client-side prediction is important because it allows the client to render the predicted outcome of a player's action immediately, improving responsiveness and reducing the perceived latency.

results.title: Some Sharp Error Bounds for Multivariate Linear Interpolation and Extrapolation - ADS
results.content:
Title: Some Sharp Error Bounds for Multivariate Linear Interpolation and Extrapolation - ADS
## ADS. ## Some Sharp Error Bounds for Multivariate Linear Interpolation and Extrapolation. #### Abstract. We study in this paper the function approximation error of linear interpolation and extrapolation. Several upper bounds are presented along with the conditions under which they are sharp. All results are under the assumptions that the function has Lipschitz continuous gradient and is interpolated on an affinely independent sample set. Errors for quadratic functions and errors of bivariate linear extrapolation are analyzed in depth. :   10.48550/arXiv.2209.12606.

results.title: Kalman filter equations and extended Kalman filter - Mostly Machine Learning
results.content: Kalman filter estimates the state of some quantities by combining two kinds of information: a dynamic model that describes our idea of how the world behaves, and measurements that provide noisy estimates of the state. * Estimate the current state $x[n,n]$ based on the (noisy) measurement and the values predicted by the dynamic model. * Predict the next state $x[n+1,n]$ based on the dynamic model equations. State update equations describe how to combine the measurements and the estimate that is obtained using our dynamic model to produce a better state estimate. The state update equation interpolates between the predicted value and the measurement. In the standard Kalman filter, the dynamic model has to be linear, meaning that it’s possible to represent the state extrapolation equation as matrix multiplication. Kalman Filter provides an estimate for the prediction error, $p$ (or generally, the covariance matrix $P$), which depends on the time instance and is updated using the covariance equations.
